surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the ligand exchange between the Ge and Se precursors with methanol co-injection. The Ge precursor reacts with methanol to form reactive intermediates such as Ge(OCH3)2, while the Se precursor reacts with methanol to form H2Se. These intermediates then react on the surface to form GeSe, with the byproducts being methanol and other volatile species.
evidence: The following reactions (1)-(3) propose a plausible mechanism to form the intermediate products, Ge(OCH3)2 and H2Se during GeSe deposition. Ge(N(Si(CH3)3)2)2 + 6CH3OH → Ge(OCH3)2 + 2NH3 + 4CH3OSi(CH3)3 (1) ((CH3)3Si)2Se + 2CH3OH → H2Se + 2CH3OSi(CH3)3 (2) Ge(OCH3)2 + H2Se → GeSe + 2CH3OH (3)
